requirements.requirement: node1 is the writable PostgreSQL primary, with node2 and node3 operating as read-only streaming standbys.
requirements.summary: node1 reported recovery=false, accepted a committed INSERT, and showed active streaming connections from both standbys. node2 and node3 reported recovery=true and transaction_read_only=on, and each directly rejected an INSERT.

requirements.requirement: Committed changes on node1 replicate to both standbys.
requirements.summary: A row committed on node1 was subsequently observed on both standbys with the same ID, payload, source, and commit timestamp.

requirements.requirement: Streaming replication uses a dedicated database network.
requirements.summary: All three nodes had active dbnet0 interfaces in 10.77.0.0/24 with peer routes and connectivity through dbnet0. PostgreSQL directly reported the standby streams using 10.77.0.2 and 10.77.0.3, while both receivers reported 10.77.0.1 as their sender.

requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL traffic is kept off the management network.
requirements.summary: PostgreSQL listened only on loopback and dbnet0 addresses, with live replication sessions using 10.77.0.x. Direct probes to all three 10.100.181.x management addresses received no PostgreSQL response, while the corresponding dbnet0 endpoints accepted connections.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct observations: node1 is writable, both read-only standbys stream and contain the committed probe row, replication uses dbnet0 addresses, and PostgreSQL is unavailable on management addresses. The only notable defect is minor temporary-file residue on node1.
limitations: The dedicated dbnet0 network is a WireGuard overlay whose tunnel endpoints use 10.100.181.x addresses. The evidence proves logical PostgreSQL endpoints and routing use dbnet0, but contains no packet capture proving that encapsulated bytes avoid the management underlay physically.
No restart or reboot was observed; persistence is supported by enabled service state but was not behaviorally tested.
Lifecycle filesystem inspection was limited to a bounded /tmp inventory, so residue elsewhere was not exhaustively assessed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Services and package state were healthy, configuration checks found no PostgreSQL or HBA errors, and required listeners were narrowly bound. Hygiene is reduced because node1 retained eight executor-created certificate and CSR artifacts under /tmp.
